paths.description: Public Turkish homepage: primary navigation, race information, news, consent and global shell.
Daily race-program information archetype, representing long tabular race content.
Horse-search/query archetype, representing the site’s data lookup journeys.
Static institutional-content archetype, also tested with JavaScript-disabled crawler rendering.
Beyaz Masa contact form: primary form, validation and recovery archetype.
English homepage locale, representing the site’s alternate-language surface.
Unknown route to assess HTTP/error recovery.

findings.summary: Consent overlay obscures the primary content on every fresh load
findings.evidence: The initial desktop screenshot shows a 275px-high cookie panel covering the entire lower portion of a 600px viewport; on the mobile capture it covers the bottom of the already scaled page.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the on-load blocking panel with a compact, accessible consent surface that does not hide core content; retain equally clear accept and reject actions.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt to the user’s dark color preference
findings.evidence: The dark-emulated screenshot is byte-identical to the ordinary desktop capture, and the computed colorScheme is “normal”.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light/dark tokens using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Transient consent and menu UI is implemented without semantic overlay primitives
findings.evidence: DOM probes found zero dialog, popover or details elements while the load screenshot displays a custom consent overlay and CSS exposes a hover-only footer dropdown.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog/popover/details as appropriate, with native focus handling and declarative dismiss behavior.

findings.summary: Long pages provide no state-aware navigation or attention cue
findings.evidence: The homepage is 2,437 CSS px tall and the race-program page is 5,655 CSS px tall, but DOM/CSS inspection found no scroll-state behavior, progress indicator or adaptive navigation chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Add unobtrusive scroll-state-aware navigation or progress cues on long information pages.

findings.summary: Mobile pages render a scaled 980px desktop canvas instead of reflowing
findings.evidence: At a requested 360x800 viewport, all four tested templates reported a 980px layout viewport and no viewport meta; the mobile screenshots show tiny desktop text and controls scaled to 36.7%.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a standards-based viewport meta tag and rebuild templates with fluid/intrinsic layout that reflows at narrow widths.

findings.summary: Reusable components do not adapt to their containers
findings.evidence: The computed probe found no container-query styling, while the same fixed-width global shell is present across homepage, query, race and form templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Use container-type and size-aware component queries for cards, tabular blocks, navigation and forms, retaining viewport queries only for page-level composition.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated and targets are too small
findings.evidence: The focus probe sampled 30 controls and every one computed outline-style none; several social links had 0x0 boxes. Lighthouse also failed target-size.
findings.suggestedFix: Add strong :focus-visible styles, remove hidden controls from the tab order, and ensure at least 24x24 CSS px spacing with larger primary targets.

findings.summary: The contact form does not expose humane validation or required-field recovery
findings.evidence: Submitting the representative Beyaz Masa form blank produced no :invalid controls and no alert/error text; most controls are not marked required despite visible required-looking personal-data fields.
findings.suggestedFix: Define constraints in HTML, validate after interaction, place actionable field errors next to inputs, and announce a summary through an aria-live region.

findings.summary: Core Web Vitals are poor under Lighthouse mobile conditions
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 3.7s and CLS 0.750, producing a 0.61 performance score; the trace corroborated LCP around 2.10s in an unthrottled headless load.
findings.suggestedFix: Identify the LCP and layout-shift sources, reserve space for late content, and prioritize only the LCP resource.

findings.summary: The critical path is large and parser-blocked
findings.evidence: HAR captured 105 requests and 3.24MB transferred. Six head stylesheets and multiple classic head scripts, including jQuery and Flowplayer, are parser-inserted with very high/high priority; five fonts/scripts lacked cache headers.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce head dependencies, defer non-critical scripts, consolidate critical CSS, apply useful caching, and remove resources not needed for first render.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused JavaScript and CSS
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 161KiB unused JavaScript and 17KiB unused CSS; duplicate Google tag bundles and a 90KiB jQuery resource dominate the waste.
findings.suggestedFix: Load analytics once, remove obsolete libraries, split by feature/template, and eliminate unused CSS rules.

findings.summary: Links, images and table data lack accessible names and relationships
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed link-name and image-alt; the images probe found 8 images without alt, the home probe found 16 links without discernible text, and Lighthouse found data cells without headers.
findings.suggestedFix: Give icon links accessible names, meaningful images alt text, and data tables explicit th/scope or headers relationships.

findings.summary: Text and navigation colors fail minimum contrast
findings.evidence: Lighthouse’s color-contrast audit failed, including white 14px navigation text on #858585 at 3.69:1 where 4.5:1 is required.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/background tokens to meet WCAG AA in every state, including navigation and disabled/secondary text.

findings.summary: Pages lack landmarks, coherent headings and visible focus
findings.evidence: The homepage probe found no main/nav/header/footer landmarks and no h1, while its first heading is h2; focus outlines are absent across sampled controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce semantic landmarks and one descriptive h1 per template, repair heading hierarchy, and add visible focus without changing logical DOM order.

findings.summary: Text and controls become illegibly small on phones
findings.evidence: The 360px captures show the full 980px desktop interface scaled to 36.7%; dense race data and form help text are too small to read comfortably.
findings.suggestedFix: Reflow content rather than scaling it, use responsive type/spacing, and simplify dense tables into readable mobile presentations.

findings.summary: Document and image asset hygiene is unsound
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported quirks-mode/no valid doctype in its tested response, deprecated APIs, incorrect image aspect ratios and low-resolution rendering. The images probe found 38/42 images without dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a consistent HTML5 doctype, remove deprecated APIs, and give images intrinsic dimensions and correct aspect ratios.

findings.summary: Indexing signals are inconsistent and stale
findings.evidence: The live pages have no canonical or hreflang links; /robots.txt returns a branded HTTP 400 page, while sitemap.xml lists legacy http:// URLs and declares a 2019 last-modified response.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a valid robots.txt, regenerate the sitemap with canonical HTTPS URLs, and add canonical/hreflang signals for Turkish and English equivalents.

findings.summary: Entity and social-share metadata is absent
findings.evidence: The organization/news homepage probe found zero JSON-LD blocks and zero Open Graph metadata despite visible organization and news entities.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/WebSite and page-specific Article structured data plus Open Graph/Twitter preview metadata.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookie attributes are incomplete
findings.evidence: HTTPS and nosniff are present, but CSP, HSTS, clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy are absent. _ga and _gid are not Secure and use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy CSP and HSTS safely, deny framing unless needed, set referrer/permissions policies, and use Secure cookies with the narrowest workable SameSite value.

findings.summary: Tracking code loads before the user has made a consent choice
findings.evidence: The load HAR includes Google Tag Manager/Analytics before consent, and tracker evidence found three known tracker origins; 90/105 requests and 3.14MB were classified outside the main www origin.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate optional analytics until consent, load one minimal analytics integration, shorten identifiers, and audit every third party for necessity.

findings.summary: Turkish pages declare English and use physical-direction CSS
findings.evidence: Every audited Turkish template declares html lang="en"; rendered CSS includes left floats/positioning and the probes report no dir attribute.
findings.suggestedFix: Set lang="tr" on Turkish pages, retain lang="en" on English pages, add hreflang, and migrate layout to logical properties.

findings.summary: Race date/time information is not explicitly locale or time-zone aware
findings.evidence: The Turkish homepage renders localized race dates and international venue schedules but exposes no machine-readable timezone, locale metadata or structured event data; the document incorrectly declares English.
findings.suggestedFix: Format from locale-aware data, attach IANA zones to event times, and expose unambiguous machine-readable dates/times.

findings.summary: Form inputs omit autocomplete and several programmatic labels
findings.evidence: The contact probe shows empty autocomplete values for name, phone, email and email confirmation; phone/email/radio/file/consent controls also lack associated labels.
findings.suggestedFix: Add correct autocomplete tokens, suitable input types/inputmode, and explicit labels/fieldsets for every control.

findings.summary: Images and third-party media consume a disproportionate resource budget
findings.evidence: Images transferred 2.62MB; all 42 inspected images use legacy formats, 21 are oversized, 30 below-fold images are not lazy-loaded and 23 lack srcset. One news image alone is 626KB.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants and srcsets, right-size thumbnails, lazy-load below-fold media, and set dimensions while preserving LCP priority.

taskList.title: Rebuild the global shell and templates for true mobile reflow
Repair semantic structure, names, labels, focus and contrast
Stop layout shifts and reserve image/content space
Optimize and responsively deliver image assets
Deploy missing security headers and secure cookie attributes
Gate and minimize analytics until consent
Replace the blocking custom consent overlay with an accessible semantic surface
Add humane form constraints, errors and autofill metadata
Correct locale, direction and event time metadata
Repair robots, sitemap, canonical, hreflang and rich metadata
Add dark-theme tokens and preference handling
